doc.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025

title: Theory, finding his own voice and learning a solo a day
summary: He says modern pedagogy hasn't influenced him; he now learns a Goodman or Fountain solo each day to develop his own ideas, as Kenny Davern urged.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: And does the theory of jazz playing play a role in the way you play? That was a lot of “plays.” And by that I mean I remember you brought up Dan Barrett. And he had a funny thing to say about modes that a student had asked him about. I’m wondering if modes and the current jazz pedagogy has any role in what you do.

I guess my honest answer is I’m not sure. I just kind of play things that speak to me, and I’m not quite sure what’s going on right now as far as currently, like in jazz academia, or what current guys are playing. So I guess in that sense it really hasn’t influenced me too much. For me personally, what I’m doing right now is I’m trying to develop more of my own ideas. And I think we’re always trying to find ways to do that, to find our own voice. I remember — I got to meet Kenny Davern about a year before he passed. And I remember he was really big on — he was very friendly to me and he was really big on finding your own voice. And it’s a hard — you’re always trying to — okay well I get the idea of finding your own voice and your own ideas and like you talk about modes and the way you play what will give you your own distinct sound. But it’s just trying to find how you do that you know. So what I found now is after a long time of listening to various different types of jazz or music and trying to learn things that maybe I don’t like stylistically but it would help me to get my mind moving in a certain direction. For instance, learning things by musicians that play more far out even though it’s hard for me to like that stuff it would help me as a player. But what I found now is you know guys like Benny and Pete Fountain and — I like their ideas the best. So what I’m doing is each day I’ll learn, just for my own enjoyment, a new solo of one of them. From start to finish. And then from that point on I’ll just start developing little ideas based on what I just learned them do. So I’m using that as kind of a template because I like what they’re doing, I like the patterns, I like the harmonies, I like the drive. And I’ll say okay, I see what they’re doing here, now I’m just going to build something of my own off of something like this. And as a result of me doing that, which I started doing back in January I’d say, it’s been as recent as that, it’s re-ignited my love for this. Because I’m having more fun now. That’s just my own little personal path — another step in finding my own personality as far as a player and — so now it’s not as much work to practice, I’m enjoying it more. Because you’ve only got so much time on this earth and I might as well just do the things I want to do.
